description:
Cross-walk of crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs (2742 lines, the canonical extension-server template per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates") against crate-jmap-chat-server/src/memory.rs confirms that BOTH patterns flagged in JMAP-x2gd.52 and .53 are workspace-canonical, not chat-server-local. The 2nd rusty pass's confidence note explicitly flagged this cross-walk as the missing exercise; now done.

Pattern 1 — Inner struct + .to_owned() HashMap key allocations:
- chat-server memory.rs:80-104 defines Inner with HashMap<(&'static str, String), HashMap<Id, Value>>
- mail-server memory.rs:109-125 defines the same nested HashMap shape
- chat-server uses .to_owned() on account_id in 6 sites (lines 110, 117, 128, 130, 139, 148)
- mail-server uses .to_owned() on account_id in 6 sites (lines 131, 138, 149, 151, 160, 207)
- Same shape, same call-site count, same hot-path-allocation idiom

Pattern 2 — query_objects pagination as-casts:
- chat-server memory.rs:603-612 uses (position as usize).min(...) and (n as usize)
- mail-server memory.rs:347-356 uses identical (position as usize).min(...) shape
- Both are clippy::cast_possible_truncation candidates; mail-server's limit cast is slightly safer (n.min(usize::MAX as u64) as usize) — see JMAP-x2gd.78 for chat-server's drift on this specific point

Pattern 3 — objects_ref / objects_mut / current_state / bump_state helpers:
- chat-server memory.rs:106-149 vs mail-server memory.rs:127-161 — identical signatures and bodies

Implications:
- JMAP-x2gd.52 (Inner HashMap-key allocations): re-classified as workspace-sweep. The fix lands in mail-server first (canonical), then propagates to chat-server, then to future siblings (calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata) when they are authored. A nested-HashMap-with-account-id-outer-key restructure on mail-server is the canonical-template change; chat-server inherits from it.
- JMAP-x2gd.53 (query pagination as-casts): re-classified as workspace-sweep. Same propagation direction.

Precedent: this matches the JMAP-x2gd.67 / .69 / .46.1 pattern for api-contract findings that turned out to be workspace-canonical.

The two original beads should remain open as 'chat-server scope' tracking; this bead is the parent for the workspace-wide sweep that lands the fix in mail-server first.
title: Workspace-canonical re-classification of JMAP-x2gd.52 and .53: mail-server memory.rs has byte-identical Inner-key-allocation + as-cast patterns
